requests.system:
Current time: <time>
Session ID: <uuid>


You are Nine operating in sub-agent mode.
You have a specific, finite task to complete. Use the available tools to
accomplish it. When done, provide a brief confirmation of what was completed.
Do not ask clarifying questions — make reasonable assumptions and proceed.


When delegating with run_agent or run_agents, pick the narrowest role that fits the task (code-reviewer, monitor, report-writer, software-dev, sysadmin); use executor only when no narrower role matches. Each role's description is in the run_agent tool schema.

## Environment

## Relevant skills
- file-management
- report-writer
- software-dev

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files in the workspace. Filter by prefix (a directory), by pattern (a glob such as *_test.go, matched against the whole path), or by changed_since (an ISO-8601 timestamp) to see what appeared or changed — including files created outside Nine, by a git pull or dropped in by a person. Each entry reports its size and whether its text is searchable.

pattern.description: Glob over the whole path, e.g. *_test.go or src/*.md.

changed_since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp; only files changed at or after it.

tools.name: skill_list
tools.description: List all available skills with their names, descriptions, and tags.

tools.name: memory_list
tools.description: List keys in the key-value store, optionally filtered by prefix.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your outstanding background jobs — handle, tool, age, and progress. Use it to see what is still running.

tools.name: goal_list
tools.description: List all goals. Call this at the start of any turn that involves open-ended, persistent work to check for active goals and recover after a restart.

tools.name: workflow_list
tools.description: List your active workflows and the 10 most recently completed ones. Call this at the start of every turn to check for in-progress work and to recover after a restart.

tools.name: tool_list
tools.description: List every tool available to you, with names and descriptions. Use this when you need the whole catalog rather than the best matches for a keyword — for example when the user asks what you can do or which tools you have. Prefer tool_search when you are looking for a specific capability.

include_schemas.description: Also return each tool's input schema (verbose; default false)

tools.name: diff_file
tools.description: Show what changed in a workspace file, as a unified diff against the version before the most recent change. Use it to report an edit back to the person you are working for, rather than describing the change in prose. Only a file that write_file, edit_file or delete_file has changed has a previous version; pass against with a trash entry name from trash_list to compare with an older one.

against.description: Trash entry name to compare against; defaults to the most recent version of this file.

tools.name: workflow_create
tools.description: Create a named workflow with an ordered list of step labels. Use this before delegating multi-step work to sub-agents. Returns a workflow_id and step IDs to reference in subsequent workflow_update calls.

steps.description: Ordered list of step labels describing the work to be done.

tools.name: job_wait
tools.description: Wait for a background job (one a long-running tool started) to finish, then return its result. If it has not finished in time, this returns its current progress instead — that is NOT an error: you can simply move on and check again later. Use the handle from when the job started, or from job_list.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before returning. Default 60.

tools.name: doc_read
tools.description: Read a section or a whole document from Nine's bundled documentation and specification. Accepts an address from doc_search ("docs/skills.md#tools"), a topic name ("agent-loop"), or a bundle path ("spec/contracts/wire-protocol"). Quote what you find rather than paraphrasing when the answer turns on exact behavior: these documents are the source of truth, and a wrong reference is a bug worth reporting.

ref.description: Section address, topic name, or bundle path

tools.name: doc_search
tools.description: Semantically search Nine's own bundled documentation and specification by a natural-language query, returning the most relevant section addresses with snippets. Use this whenever a question is about how Nine itself works — its architecture, configuration, tools, wire protocol, or terminology — before answering from memory. Then doc_read the address for the exact text.

query.description: What you want to know about Nine

bundle.description: Restrict to the user documentation or the specification; omit to search both

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Retrieve a value from the key-value store by key.

tools.name: memory_set
tools.description: Store a value in the key-value store.

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description: Delete a key from the key-value store.

tools.name: file_search_text
tools.description: Full-text search over stored file content. Pass path to search inside one file (or one directory prefix) — the way to find the relevant region of a large spilled tool output.

path.description: Restrict the search to paths starting with this prefix; omit to search all files.

tools.name: skill_read
tools.description: Read the full content of a skill by name.

tools.name: skill_write
tools.description: Create or replace one of your own skills (a markdown how-to note). Built-in skills are read-only and cannot be overwritten.

tools.name: skill_modify
tools.description: Update one of your own skills, replacing description, tags, and/or content as provided. Built-in skills cannot be modified.

tools.name: capability_request
tools.description: Ask the operator to grant a capability the generated-tool ceiling does not currently permit. Use this when writing a tool failed because a capability is not available on this instance: the request is queued for a human, who approves or denies it. Approval takes effect without a restart, so retry the write after one is granted. Requesting does not grant — you never confer a capability on yourself.

capability.description: The capability to request, exactly as the refusal named it.

reason.description: Why the task cannot be done without it. A human reads this and nothing else about your intent, so be specific about what the tool does with the reach.

tool_name.description: The tool that needs it, if you have already named one.

params.description: What the capability should be scoped to, narrowest that works. For net.http: {"allow_hosts":["api.example.com"],"methods":["GET"]}. For env: {"env":["TZ"]}. For fs: {"mounts":[{"host":"/srv/data","guest":"/data"}]}. A broad request is likelier to be denied.

tools.name: queued_messages_get
tools.description: Read all messages currently queued for this session. Returns messages with their consumption status. Queued messages are user replies that were added while the session was busy, and are NOT automatically included in the model's context. Each message has a 'consumed' field indicating whether it has been processed. Use queued_message_mark_consumed to mark individual messages as consumed after processing them.

tools.name: queued_message_mark_consumed
tools.description: Mark a specific queued message as consumed by its index. Once marked as consumed, the message will be moved to conversation history and appear in future context. This allows fine-grained control: you can process some messages and leave others in the queue.

index.description: 0-based index of the message to mark as consumed

tools.name: queued_messages_mark_all_consumed
tools.description: Mark all queued messages as consumed. This moves all messages to conversation history so they will appear in future context as normal user messages.

tools.name: queued_messages_count
tools.description: Get the number of messages currently queued for this session (including both consumed and unconsumed).

tools.name: queued_messages_unconsumed_count
tools.description: Get the number of unconsumed messages currently queued for this session.

tools.name: skill_search
tools.description: Semantically search available skills by a natural-language query, returning the most relevant skill names and descriptions. Use this to find a skill when you do not know its exact name or when the task changes; then skill_read the one you want.

tools.name: run_agent
tools.description: Spawn a sub-agent to execute a single self-contained task and return its final answer. Use this to isolate a focused piece of work or delegate a subtask. For multiple independent tasks at once, use run_agents.

task.description: A clear, self-contained description of the task for the sub-agent.

context.description: Optional background the sub-agent needs. Keep concise.

role.description: Optional worker role for the sub-agent. One of: code-reviewer: Review code without changing it — file reads, text search, and diffs. No shell, no writes | executor (default): Default leaf worker for delegated tasks — full toolset, may sub-delegate within the depth cap | monitor: Read-only standing-agent worker — web, HTTP GET, file reads, and memory; no shell, no writes | report-writer: Research and write — web search, page reading, and workspace files; no shell | software-dev: Implement and modify code — edit files, run builds and tests via shell | sysadmin: Inspect and operate the system — shell, file edits, and HTTP calls for ops tasks. Pick the narrowest role that fits the task; omit for executor. Unknown roles fall back to executor.

tools.name: run_agents
tools.description: Spawn multiple sub-agents in parallel and wait for all results. Use this when tasks are independent and can run concurrently. Returns when all agents finish or the timeout expires.

role.description: Optional worker role for the sub-agent. One of: code-reviewer: Review code without changing it — file reads, text search, and diffs. No shell, no writes | executor (default): Default leaf worker for delegated tasks — full toolset, may sub-delegate within the depth cap | monitor: Read-only standing-agent worker — web, HTTP GET, file reads, and memory; no shell, no writes | report-writer: Research and write — web search, page reading, and workspace files; no shell | software-dev: Implement and modify code — edit files, run builds and tests via shell | sysadmin: Inspect and operate the system — shell, file edits, and HTTP calls for ops tasks. Pick the narrowest role that fits the task; omit for executor. Unknown roles fall back to executor.

timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds to wait for the whole group. Defaults to the daemon's configured task timeout (typically 30 minutes); only lower this if the tasks are known to be quick. Agents still running when the timeout fires are cancelled and marked timed_out.

tools.name: workflow_get
tools.description: Get the full plan and current step statuses for a workflow by ID.

tools.name: workflow_update
tools.description: Update a workflow step's status after work completes. When all steps reach a terminal status the workflow closes automatically.

tools.name: workflow_retry_step
tools.description: Reset a failed step to pending and immediately re-run it with a new sub-agent.

tools.name: goal_create
tools.description: Create a persistent, open-ended goal (no defined end condition, e.g. 'monitor this repo for security issues'). Defaults to the current conversation as parent if parent_id is omitted. Returns the created goal; top-level goals (parent_type 'conversation') also get a background 'pursue' session that works on the goal between your turns — the response's pursue_session field is 'spawned' if that session started, or 'limit_reached' if the daemon is already at its concurrent goal-session cap (the goal is still recorded either way).

parent_id.description: ID of the conversation or goal that spawned this one. Defaults to the current conversation.

parent_type.description: Type of the parent referenced by parent_id.

tools.name: goal_get
tools.description: Get a goal by ID, including its status and sub-goal/task tree.

tools.name: goal_update_status
tools.description: Update a goal's status.

status.description: active = in progress, paused = temporarily on hold, done = completed or resolved, archived = retired without completion.

tools.name: tool_search
tools.description: Semantically search the tools available to you by a natural-language query, returning the most relevant tool names, descriptions, and input schemas. Use this when the tools you can currently see do not fit the task — a relevant tool may exist that was not surfaced up front. Call the returned tool directly by its name.

query.description: What capability you are looking for

tools.name: job_check
tools.description: Return a background job's current state and progress — and its result if it has finished — without waiting. Use it to poll a job you are not blocking on.

tools.name: job_cancel
tools.description: Request cancellation of a background job. Best-effort; the job stops as soon as the plugin notices.

tools.name: trash_list
tools.description: List files recoverable from the trash, newest first: everything delete_file removed and every version write_file or edit_file replaced. Pass path to narrow to a path fragment. Each result names a trash entry to hand to restore_file.

path.description: Only entries whose original path contains this text.

tools.name: process_list
tools.description: List the processes running in the background — goal sessions, standing agents, reflection, watchers, standing tools — with each one's state, trigger and budget use. Use it to see what runs between conversations.

tools.name: restore_file
tools.description: Restore a file from the trash to the workspace, by the entry name trash_list reports. Restores to its original path unless to names another. Never overwrites: if something already occupies the destination the call fails, since recovering one file by destroying another is not a recovery.

entry.description: Trash entry name from trash_list, e.g. 20260920T143015Z-1f2e3d4c.

path.description: Which file to restore, when the entry holds more than one.

to.description: Destination path; defaults to where the file came from.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Delete one file, or one empty directory, from the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. The file is moved to Nine's trash rather than destroyed, so a mistake can be undone with trash_list and restore_file until the trash is swept. There is no recursive delete: delete a directory's contents first. Prefer this over `rm` in the shell, which destroys a file outright.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write content to a file on the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM, creating parent directories as needed. To copy a large payload — a spilled tool result, typically — pass content_ref with its path instead of content, and the bytes never enter your context. Paths resolve under /work. Replaces the file whole: to change part of an existing file use edit_file, and to add to the end pass mode=append. A file written here is full-text searchable with file_search_text once the workspace scan sees it.

mode.description: replace (default) rewrites the file; append adds to the end without reading it.

if_unchanged.description: A version token from read_file. The write fails if the file changed since then.

preview.description: Return the diff this write would make and write nothing.

content_ref.description: A path whose content to write here — a spill/... path from a truncated tool result, or another workspace file. Used instead of content; the data never passes through your context.

tools.name: copy_file
tools.description: Copy a file inside the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. The contents stream from one path to the other without passing through your context, so a large file costs nothing to duplicate. Refuses an existing destination unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it exists (default false).

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move or rename a file inside the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. The file is relinked, not copied and not read, so this costs nothing for a large file and never spends context on its contents. Refuses an existing destination unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it exists (default false).

tools.name: process_send
tools.description: Send a message to a running live process; it receives it as its next trigger. It does not wait for an answer: the process answers through what it writes — files, memory, the notification feed. Refused when the process is stopped, busy, or a slice process with no session.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file from the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. Paths resolve under /work; a relative path is taken as relative to it. Read part of a large file with lines ("120-180") or with offset and limit, rather than pulling the whole thing into context. Pass line_numbers when you intend to edit, so you can name the exact text for edit_file. A windowed read also returns a version token for write_file's if_unchanged. A spill/... path from a truncated tool result is read with this same tool.

path.description: Path under the workspace, e.g. notes.txt or /work/notes.txt

lines.description: 1-based inclusive line range, e.g. "120-180" or "120". Preferred over offset/limit for text.

limit.description: Maximum bytes to return; omit or 0 for the rest of the file.

line_numbers.description: Prefix each line with its number.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace exact text in a WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM file, leaving the rest byte-for-byte unchanged. Use this rather than write_file whenever the file already exists: it never loads the file into your context, so it works on a file far larger than your context window. old_text must match the file exactly, including indentation and line breaks — read the region with read_file(lines) first. The call fails, changing nothing, when the number of matches is not what you said to expect.

old_text.description: Exact text to replace. Include enough surrounding lines to make it unique.

new_text.description: Replacement text. Empty deletes the matched text.

expect.description: How many occurrences to replace: a positive integer (default 1), or "all".

preview.description: Return the diff this edit would make and write nothing.

tools.name: http_get
tools.description: Fetch a URL and return its status and body.

tools.name: http_post
tools.description: POST a body to a URL and return the status and response.

tools.name: time
tools.description: Return the current date and time in UTC (ISO-8601 and a readable form).

tools.name: web_page_read
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its readable text, with markup and scripts stripped.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return result titles, URLs, and snippets. Uses DuckDuckGo by default; set SEARCH_PROVIDER=brave|serpapi and SEARCH_API_KEY for another backend.

tools.name: process_show
tools.description: Show one process in detail: its state and who stopped it, its trigger, session, goal and pipe, its budget use and when that resets, its last error, and its recent activity.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.

tools.name: process_start
tools.description: Start a stopped process. It runs under its own grants, role and budget, so starting it grants nothing new. Refused for a process the operator stopped, one its goal stopped (reactivate the goal instead), one paused by its budget until the budget resets, and at the running-process cap.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.

tools.name: process_stop
tools.description: Stop a process. A model may start it again later; one the operator stops only the operator can.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.

tools.name: trash_list
tools.description: List files recoverable from the trash, newest first: everything delete_file removed and every version write_file or edit_file replaced. Pass path to narrow to a path fragment. Each result names a trash entry to hand to restore_file.

path.description: Only entries whose original path contains this text.

tools.name: process_list
tools.description: List the processes running in the background — goal sessions, standing agents, reflection, watchers, standing tools — with each one's state, trigger and budget use. Use it to see what runs between conversations.

tools.name: restore_file
tools.description: Restore a file from the trash to the workspace, by the entry name trash_list reports. Restores to its original path unless to names another. Never overwrites: if something already occupies the destination the call fails, since recovering one file by destroying another is not a recovery.

entry.description: Trash entry name from trash_list, e.g. 20260920T143015Z-1f2e3d4c.

path.description: Which file to restore, when the entry holds more than one.

to.description: Destination path; defaults to where the file came from.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Delete one file, or one empty directory, from the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. The file is moved to Nine's trash rather than destroyed, so a mistake can be undone with trash_list and restore_file until the trash is swept. There is no recursive delete: delete a directory's contents first. Prefer this over `rm` in the shell, which destroys a file outright.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write content to a file on the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM, creating parent directories as needed. To copy a large payload — a spilled tool result, typically — pass content_ref with its path instead of content, and the bytes never enter your context. Paths resolve under /work. Replaces the file whole: to change part of an existing file use edit_file, and to add to the end pass mode=append. A file written here is full-text searchable with file_search_text once the workspace scan sees it.

mode.description: replace (default) rewrites the file; append adds to the end without reading it.

if_unchanged.description: A version token from read_file. The write fails if the file changed since then.

preview.description: Return the diff this write would make and write nothing.

content_ref.description: A path whose content to write here — a spill/... path from a truncated tool result, or another workspace file. Used instead of content; the data never passes through your context.

tools.name: copy_file
tools.description: Copy a file inside the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. The contents stream from one path to the other without passing through your context, so a large file costs nothing to duplicate. Refuses an existing destination unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it exists (default false).

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move or rename a file inside the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. The file is relinked, not copied and not read, so this costs nothing for a large file and never spends context on its contents. Refuses an existing destination unless overwrite is true.

overwrite.description: Replace the destination if it exists (default false).

tools.name: process_send
tools.description: Send a message to a running live process; it receives it as its next trigger. It does not wait for an answer: the process answers through what it writes — files, memory, the notification feed. Refused when the process is stopped, busy, or a slice process with no session.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file from the WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM. Paths resolve under /work; a relative path is taken as relative to it. Read part of a large file with lines ("120-180") or with offset and limit, rather than pulling the whole thing into context. Pass line_numbers when you intend to edit, so you can name the exact text for edit_file. A windowed read also returns a version token for write_file's if_unchanged. A spill/... path from a truncated tool result is read with this same tool.

path.description: Path under the workspace, e.g. notes.txt or /work/notes.txt

lines.description: 1-based inclusive line range, e.g. "120-180" or "120". Preferred over offset/limit for text.

limit.description: Maximum bytes to return; omit or 0 for the rest of the file.

line_numbers.description: Prefix each line with its number.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace exact text in a WORKSPACE FILESYSTEM file, leaving the rest byte-for-byte unchanged. Use this rather than write_file whenever the file already exists: it never loads the file into your context, so it works on a file far larger than your context window. old_text must match the file exactly, including indentation and line breaks — read the region with read_file(lines) first. The call fails, changing nothing, when the number of matches is not what you said to expect.

old_text.description: Exact text to replace. Include enough surrounding lines to make it unique.

new_text.description: Replacement text. Empty deletes the matched text.

expect.description: How many occurrences to replace: a positive integer (default 1), or "all".

preview.description: Return the diff this edit would make and write nothing.

tools.name: http_get
tools.description: Fetch a URL and return its status and body.

tools.name: http_post
tools.description: POST a body to a URL and return the status and response.

tools.name: time
tools.description: Return the current date and time in UTC (ISO-8601 and a readable form).

tools.name: web_page_read
tools.description: Fetch a web page and return its readable text, with markup and scripts stripped.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web and return result titles, URLs, and snippets. Uses DuckDuckGo by default; set SEARCH_PROVIDER=brave|serpapi and SEARCH_API_KEY for another backend.

tools.name: process_show
tools.description: Show one process in detail: its state and who stopped it, its trigger, session, goal and pipe, its budget use and when that resets, its last error, and its recent activity.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.

tools.name: process_start
tools.description: Start a stopped process. It runs under its own grants, role and budget, so starting it grants nothing new. Refused for a process the operator stopped, one its goal stopped (reactivate the goal instead), one paused by its budget until the budget resets, and at the running-process cap.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.

tools.name: process_stop
tools.description: Stop a process. A model may start it again later; one the operator stops only the operator can.

id.description: The process id, as process_list shows it.
